QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_8

question.text: Under the SAS framework, if an SIA is asked to express an opinion on the monetary SROI ratio of a programme, what level of assurance is typically permitted?

answer.text: Limited assurance only (expressed as a negative-assurance conclusion)
No assurance is permitted on SROI — only on activities and outputs
Both reasonable and limited assurance, depending on evidence sufficiency and engagement scope

explanation.text: The Logic: The SAS framework allows both limited and reasonable assurance depending on the evidence base. SROI ratios depend on assumption-heavy proxies (e.g., shadow prices for water, health-year valuations); limited assurance is typical, reasonable only where robust counterfactual data is available. The SIA chooses based on evidence sufficiency. The Trap: Options A and B are too narrow. Option C overstates — SROI CAN be reported, but with full disclosure of assumptions and deadweight. Cross-Exam Context: Two-tier assurance parallels III-A / III-C Compliance chapters on sustainability / BRSR assurance tiers and the review-vs-audit distinction in general assurance frameworks. Assessor's Pro-Tip: If the SE pushes for reasonable assurance on SROI, check whether the control group / counterfactual is defensible — if not, step down to limited assurance and document the reason in the engagement letter.
